text:
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins missed more than two weeks after leaving a Nov. 7 game in Vancouver early, and he returned Nov. 24 against Vegas. Before that he was humming: 11 points in 13 games, seven on the power play. He has now gone five straight games without a point, a stretch that includes the night he left early.

Our read is mixed. The drought isn't a case of bad luck, because his chances thinned out over that stretch (3.5 expected points in the five games). But across the season his own shooting sits right where his expected goals say it should (4 goals on 4.17), and Edmonton has scored 4.3 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. Evolving-Hockey's numbers last season put most of his value on the power play, which is still his clearest job. Daily Faceoff Edmonton's Oilersnation posted that "The Oilers may have found a second line in Dach, Nugent-Hopkins, and Kapanen." Our numbers project 51 points. Watch whether that line holds together.
headline: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins is back, and searching for points
